objectives: To evaluate and synthesize the existing evidence on factors influencing the quality of life (QoL) of non-Hodgkin lymphoma survivors, and to comprehensively understand how these factors affect QoL after completion of primary treatment.
inclusion_criteria: Eligible studies involved adults aged >=18 years; were original quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-methods studies; investigated factors influencing QoL among non-Hodgkin lymphoma survivors; included participants diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma after completion of primary treatment; could be conducted in any setting (inpatient, outpatient, or home); were reported in English; and, per the review's search limits/update, fell within the 2014-2025 publication window.
exclusion_criteria: Excluded were studies that did not include the population of interest, involved animal subjects, or included Hodgkin lymphoma/non-Hodgkin lymphoma survivors who were still receiving treatment or had recurrent disease. The authors also excluded non-English studies and nonoriginal/noneligible publication types, including conference proceedings, abstracts, review articles, theoretical studies, pilot studies, protocols, dissertations, letters to the editor, opinion/viewpoint pieces, statement articles, government documents, and working papers.
pmid_query: (hematologic*[Title/Abstract] OR haematologic*[Title/Abstract] OR lymphoma*[Title/Abstract] OR "non-Hodgkin lymphoma"[Title/Abstract] OR "non-Hodgkin lymphoma survivors"[Title/Abstract]) AND ("quality of life"[Title/Abstract] OR factors[Title/Abstract] OR "physical well-being"[Title/Abstract] OR "psychological well-being"[Title/Abstract] OR "emotional well-being"[Title/Abstract] OR "functional well-being"[Title/Abstract]) AND English[Language] AND ("2014/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2025/12/31"[Date - Publication])
selection_evidence: Results/PRISMA state that 898 records were identified, 174 duplicates were removed, 35 full texts were assessed, 16 were excluded, and 19 studies were finally included. Main Table 1 summarizes characteristics for exactly 19 included studies. Supplementary Table 1 (MOESM4_ESM; titled 'Summary Table 19 Studies') enumerates exactly 19 included-study entries, labeled with the manuscript's reference numbers as Study 12, Study 14, and Study 20 through Study 36. Cross-checking against the numbered reference list shows these labels map to published journal articles, while non-study/non-literature references are not part of the included-study table.
notes: The PMID query is reconstructed from the manuscript's explicit Boolean search terms, English-language restriction, and publication-year limits because the article/supplements do not provide a database-specific PubMed search string. Git was unavailable in this environment, so staged-file inspection could not be performed; the analysis relied on the provided on-disk target files and supplemental text extracts.
